subject: Evaluation — Evidence-Based Scoring of Completed Artifacts and Agent Deliverables
description: Application-shape eval set for evaluation (SH-6337 batch 5). Tests whether loading the evaluation skill changes how a model scores a completed deliverable — specifically: applying the skeptical-critic stance, identifying score ceilings from missing evidence, distinguishing tests-passing from acceptance-criteria-complete, and routing away from evaluation when the task is diff review, eval-dataset design, or methodology design. 5 real cases (skill SHOULD change verdict or score) + 2 red-herring probes (line-by-line diff review / designing a new eval dataset — skill should NOT fire or should explicitly defer to code-review / agent-eval-design). Scenarios are portable and principle-grounded; no internal codebase data.

cases.scenario:
An agent completed a task to 'add pagination to the orders table'. The agent's completion report states:

'Task complete. I added a pagination component to the orders table. TypeScript compiles, ESLint passes, all 14 existing tests pass. The new pagination renders correctly at 1920px viewport.'

The original task specification included the following acceptance criteria:
- [ ] Table displays 25 rows per page by default
- [ ] Page count adjusts when filters reduce the result set
- [ ] Keyboard navigation (Left/Right arrow keys) advances pages
- [ ] Mobile viewport (375px) shows a compact pagination variant
- [ ] URL query param `?page=N` preserves pagination state on reload

The agent's report does not mention any of these criteria.
cases.context: The agent has claimed completion based on TypeScript, lint, and existing-test checks. The acceptance criteria listed in the task were never verified. The agent's report provides evidence for code correctness but not for acceptance-criteria satisfaction.
cases.question: Evaluate this completion claim. What score would you assign, and what is the honest verdict?
expected_flags: the agent has verified code quality (TypeScript, lint, tests) but not acceptance-criteria satisfaction — these are different questions; the criteria listed (default page size, filter adjustment, keyboard navigation, mobile variant, URL state) are none of them covered in the evidence provided
a score ceiling applies: without evidence that any of the 5 acceptance criteria are met, the honest score cannot exceed 1-2 out of 5, regardless of TypeScript and lint passing
this is an optimistic completion claim: 'task complete' is stated before any of the acceptance criteria are checked; the evidence packet is incomplete
expected_fix_hints: re-evaluate each acceptance criterion with direct evidence: run the app, verify default page size is 25, test filter impact on page count, test keyboard navigation with Tab/Arrow keys, test at 375px viewport, test reload with ?page=2 in the URL
for each criterion either provide evidence it is met (screenshot, test output, reproduction step) or mark it as not yet verified and return score accordingly
score should be: 1-2 (work started but acceptance criteria unverified) until each criterion is checked — do not move to 4-5 until all 5 are verified
absent_signals: should NOT accept 'TypeScript compiles, ESLint passes, tests pass' as sufficient evidence for calling an acceptance-criteria-specified task complete
should NOT score this higher than 2 out of 5 given zero evidence for any acceptance criterion
should NOT treat 'renders correctly at 1920px' as addressing the mobile viewport criterion — it verifies desktop only

cases.scenario:
A documentation update task requested: 'Update the API reference for the /orders endpoint to reflect the new `fulfillment_status` field added in v2.3.'

The agent's completion report states:
'Updated the API reference. The fulfillment_status field is now documented with its type (string) and example values (pending, fulfilled, cancelled).'

The acceptance criteria included:
- [ ] Field documented with type, allowed values, and deprecation note if applicable
- [ ] Example request/response bodies updated to include the new field
- [ ] Changelog entry added for v2.3
- [ ] Any downstream docs that reference the orders response shape are updated

The agent updated one section of the reference but did not mention example bodies, a changelog entry, or downstream doc checks.
cases.context: The documentation update is partially complete. The agent documented the field type and values (criterion 1 partially met) but criteria 2, 3, and 4 have no evidence.
cases.question: Score this documentation update deliverable honestly. What evidence is missing, and what is the score ceiling?
expected_flags: the score ceiling is 2 out of 5: criterion 1 is partially met (type and values documented, but no deprecation note mentioned even though the criteria require checking); criteria 2, 3, and 4 have zero evidence
the absence of evidence for the changelog entry is a gap, not a low-severity finding — changelogs are a delivery contract in API documentation; missing them causes consumer confusion on version bumps
downstream doc updates (criterion 4) require an explicit check; the agent's report contains no grep or search evidence that downstream pages were checked
expected_fix_hints: add example request/response bodies showing the field in both the request (if applicable) and a successful response
add a changelog entry under v2.3: 'Added `fulfillment_status` field to /orders response — possible values: pending, fulfilled, cancelled'
grep docs for any page that references the /orders response schema and verify they reflect the new field; report the paths checked and any that needed updating
absent_signals: should NOT score this as 4 or 5 just because the field was added to one section of the reference
should NOT treat 'type and example values documented' as fully satisfying criterion 1 without checking the deprecation note requirement
should NOT assume that downstream docs were implicitly checked because the agent mentioned updating 'the API reference'

cases.scenario:
A task to 'write an integration test for the order-export service' produced the following completion report:

'Test written and passing. The test verifies that calling exportOrders() with a date range returns a non-empty CSV string.'

The original acceptance criteria were:
- [ ] Test covers the happy path: valid date range returns a CSV with correct headers and at least one row
- [ ] Test covers the empty-results case: date range with no orders returns an empty CSV with headers only
- [ ] Test covers the error case: invalid date format raises an explicit error with a descriptive message
- [ ] Test runs in the CI pipeline without additional environment setup
cases.context: The agent wrote one test case covering the happy path partially. The empty-results case, the error case, and CI compatibility are not addressed. The report provides one test case as evidence.
cases.question: Is the evidence sufficient to call this task complete? What is missing?
expected_flags: the agent tested happy-path only and partially — 'non-empty CSV string' confirms data exists but does not verify correct headers, which is part of criterion 1
the empty-results case (criterion 2) and the error case for invalid date format (criterion 3) have no test; the report does not mention them

CI pipeline compatibility (criterion 4) has no evidence — 'test passing' in a local dev environment may not mean the test passes in CI if it has environment dependencies (database, env vars, credentials)
expected_fix_hints: add a test case for the empty-results scenario: exportOrders() with a date range that returns zero records should produce a CSV with headers only, not an empty string
add a test case for the error scenario: calling exportOrders() with an invalid date format (e.g., '2024-13-45') should throw an error with a descriptive message, not silently return empty output
verify the test runs in CI: check that the test file is included in the test runner's glob pattern, that any required database or service is available in CI, and report the CI environment setup
absent_signals: should NOT call this complete with one partial happy-path test case out of four criteria
should NOT treat 'test passing locally' as equivalent to 'runs in CI pipeline without additional setup'
should NOT score this as 3 or above — one of four criteria is partially met; maximum honest score is 2

cases.scenario:
A task asked to 'implement rate limiting on the /api/export endpoint to prevent abuse'. The agent's completion report says:

'Implemented rate limiting: 100 requests per minute per IP address using an in-memory store. TypeScript passes, unit tests pass. Tested manually against localhost.'

The acceptance criteria specified:
- [ ] Rate limit applied per authenticated user (not per IP)
- [ ] Rate limit state persists across server restarts
- [ ] Rate limit is configurable via environment variable
- [ ] Behavior is documented in the API reference

The agent used per-IP limiting with an in-memory store.
cases.context: The implementation is technically functional but misaligned with the acceptance criteria on two fundamental design decisions: per-IP vs per-user, and in-memory (ephemeral) vs persistent store. The agent's report does not acknowledge the misalignment.
cases.question: Evaluate this implementation against the acceptance criteria. What is the verdict, and what are the residual risks?
expected_flags: per-IP rate limiting fails criterion 1: users behind NAT or VPN share an IP, so the limit applies incorrectly; authenticated users from different IPs bypass each other's limits

in-memory store fails criterion 2: the rate limit state is lost on server restart, allowing a burst of requests immediately after any deploy or crash — this is a reliability gap in a security-relevant feature
criteria 3 (environment variable configuration) and 4 (API reference documentation) have no evidence in the completion report
residual risk: in production, a user could intentionally trigger a server restart to reset their rate limit count — the in-memory store is not acceptable for a security gate
expected_fix_hints: change the rate limit key from IP to authenticated user ID: extract the user from the session or JWT and key the limit on user ID, not IP
replace the in-memory store with a persistent store: Redis is the standard choice for distributed rate limiting; at minimum use a database row with a TTL
add an environment variable (e.g., EXPORT_RATE_LIMIT_RPM=100) with documentation in the API reference and .env.example
mark this as BLOCK or requires revision — the implementation does not meet criteria 1 or 2, which are the security-relevant ones
absent_signals: should NOT accept 'TypeScript passes, unit tests pass' as completion evidence for a security feature with misaligned design decisions
should NOT score this above 1 — the fundamental design decisions (per-IP, in-memory) conflict with the first two acceptance criteria
should NOT treat the manual localhost test as evidence that the feature works correctly in a multi-server production environment

cases.scenario:
An agent evaluation of a skill-upgrade task returned a score of 3 out of 5 with the following findings:

Finding 1 (REQUIRED): The new Understanding fields (mental_model, purpose, boundary, analogy, misconception) are present but the 'boundary' field describes what the skill IS for rather than what it is NOT for — it is inverted relative to the field semantics.
Finding 2 (REQUIRED): The eval_artifacts field was changed to 'present' but no evals.json file was added to the commit.
Finding 3 (ADVISORY): The description field's negative boundary clause is 45 words; the style guide recommends under 30.

The agent revised the skill and produced a new version. The revision report states: 'Fixed Finding 1 and Finding 3. Finding 2 is not applicable — the evals.json is in a separate PR.'

The task instruction was: 'All required findings must be resolved in this PR before merging.'
cases.context: The revision resolved one of the two required findings (Finding 1) and the advisory finding (Finding 3). The agent is claiming Finding 2 is 'not applicable' by deferring it to a separate PR, but the task instruction explicitly required all required findings to be resolved before merge.
cases.question: Is the revised skill complete? Does the evaluation verdict change from 3 to pass?
expected_flags: Finding 2 is REQUIRED and unresolved — setting eval_artifacts to 'present' without committing an evals.json is a doc lie (the field claims evidence exists that does not exist); deferring to a separate PR does not resolve it in this change
the task instruction ('all required findings must be resolved in this PR') makes this a blocking condition — the agent's 'not applicable' claim contradicts the explicit task gate
the revised score should remain BLOCK or 2 at most: one required finding fixed, one required finding deferred but not resolved
expected_fix_hints: either add a minimal evals.json to this commit (satisfying the eval_artifacts: present claim) or revert eval_artifacts to 'planned' so the claim matches reality
do not accept 'in a separate PR' as resolution of a REQUIRED finding that was identified within this task's scope — the resolution must be in this change
re-score the revision after Finding 2 is actually resolved: once evals.json exists or eval_artifacts is corrected, the verdict can advance to PASS
absent_signals: should NOT accept 'not applicable' as resolution of a REQUIRED finding
should NOT advance the verdict from 3 to PASS while a REQUIRED finding is deferred
should NOT treat the advisory-finding resolution (Finding 3 — description word count) as compensating for the unresolved required finding (Finding 2)

cases.scenario:
A senior engineer asks: 'Here's the diff from the pull request that adds the order-export service. Can you review it line by line? I'm specifically looking for any security issues in the authorization check and any N+1 query patterns in the database access layer.'

The diff is 340 lines across 4 files.
cases.context: This is a line-by-line pull request review request focused on security and performance concerns in a specific diff. The task is code inspection, not completion scoring of a deliverable.
cases.question: What is wrong with this authorization check and are there N+1 query patterns in the database layer?
expected_flags: this is a code-review task — inspecting a diff for security vulnerabilities and performance anti-patterns in a specific PR — not an evaluation of a completed deliverable against acceptance criteria
the evaluation skill (skeptical-critic stance, 1-5 scoring, score ceilings, acceptance-criteria verification) does not apply here; this belongs to the code-review skill
expected_fix_hints: route to code-review for this task: look for missing authentication/authorization guards, validate that orgQuery() is used instead of query() for tenant-bound routes, check for loops over database results that trigger additional queries per iteration
do not apply a 1-5 evaluation score or score ceiling to a diff review — evaluation scores apply to completed deliverables, not to open PRs being inspected for issues
absent_signals: should NOT produce a 1-5 completion score or acceptance-criteria verification table for a diff review request
should NOT apply the 'skeptical critic stance on whether work is done' lens — the work is explicitly in-progress and under review
should NOT route this to the evaluation skill's completion-gate pattern; this is code-review territory

cases.scenario:
A team building an AI coding agent wants to test whether the agent correctly handles edge cases in SQL generation. They ask: 'Design a set of eval cases for our SQL-generation agent. We need cases that test: (1) the agent's ability to handle JOINs with NULL-producing rows, (2) GROUP BY with HAVING clauses, and (3) subquery vs CTE preference. Include hard negatives where the agent's SQL would produce the wrong result.'

They want the eval cases written in a structured format so they can run them against the agent automatically.
cases.context: This is a task to design a new evaluation dataset with graders and hard negatives for an AI agent — not a task to evaluate a specific existing deliverable. The output requested is a structured eval corpus.
cases.question: Design the eval cases and hard negatives for the SQL-generation agent.
expected_flags: this is an eval-dataset design task, not a deliverable evaluation task — the output is a new eval corpus (cases, graders, expected outputs, hard negatives), not a score or verdict on existing work

this belongs to the agent-eval-design skill, which covers creating eval suites, designing graders, and writing hard negatives; the evaluation skill scores existing artifacts and does not design new eval datasets
expected_fix_hints: route to agent-eval-design for this task: design the eval format (input query, expected SQL, grader check), write the three case categories (NULL-producing JOINs, GROUP BY + HAVING, subquery vs CTE), include at least one hard negative per category (a plausible SQL that returns wrong results for a common edge case)
do not apply the evaluation skill's completion-scoring rubric to this task — there is no existing deliverable to score; the task is to author the corpus
absent_signals: should NOT produce a 1-5 completion score for the SQL-generation agent before any eval has been run
should NOT apply the acceptance-criteria verification table pattern to this task — no acceptance criteria for a specific deliverable exist here
should NOT conflate evaluation (scoring existing work) with eval-dataset design (creating the apparatus that will enable future evaluation)
